assets.title: Test events can only prove so much
assets.content:
Subject: Test events can only prove so much
Preview text: Verify instrumentation and handlers, not production deliverability.

Hi there,

Sending the same harmless payload to three Resend test addresses lets you inspect delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint paths before using real recipients. Only the recipient changes.

Resend is an email sending platform for transactional email. Send one message at a time to delivered@resend.dev, bounced@resend.dev, and complained@resend.dev, then compare the resulting events in the Emails Dashboard.

If you already have a public endpoint and webhook configured, you can also confirm that each JSON event reaches the intended handler.

This test checks event instrumentation and handler behavior without affecting domain reputation. It does not establish production deliverability with real mailbox providers.

Review the test-address documentation →

- the Resend team

The email only conditionally says my application may need to handle these outcomes, which is reasonable. It does not establish that I am evaluating Resend, use Supabase Auth, have a current rate-limit problem, or need a new provider; those remain unknown.

Reading emphasis: scrutinise whether the claims earn trust for the requested next step. Do not invent a prior purchase, failed tool or bad experience; distinguish trying the product from adopting it in production.

assets.title: A delivered test is only one path
assets.content:
Subject: A delivered test is only one path
Preview text: Compare it with Resend’s bounce and spam-complaint simulations before an integration test.

Hi there,

A useful evaluation starts with a narrower question: can you clearly distinguish the outcomes your application may need to handle?

Resend is an email API for sending transactional messages and inspecting their lifecycle through its Dashboard, API, and webhooks.

Its documentation provides test addresses for delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint outcomes. Send one minimal payload to each address, changing only the recipient, then compare the associated events in the Emails Dashboard.

That comparison helps you decide whether Resend exposes the three simulated outcomes clearly enough to proceed with a small integration test and define your event handling.

The sends do not affect domain reputation, but count against your account quota. They do not establish production deliverability or inbox placement, and Dashboard inspection alone does not validate an application webhook path.

Review the documented test →

- the Resend team
